AbandonResponse.description:
What was torn down, plus the children triage list.

Blocking children existed only for this parent, so the owner disposes each; parallel children
continue untouched.
AbandonResponse.title: AbandonResponse

AboutRow.description:
One row of `About this work-item`, in the owner's own framing.

A LIST, not an object: the order is the meaning. An empty row is dropped server-side.
AboutRow.title: AboutRow

AgentModelRow.description:
One tunable background sub-agent: the TIER it tracks, and the concrete model that tier currently
resolves to.
AgentModelRow.title: AgentModelRow

ArchivedRepoTokens.description:
One disconnected project's preserved spend. `label` is the tombstoned display name, falling back
to the bare id.
ArchivedRepoTokens.title: ArchivedRepoTokens

ArchivedTokens.description:
Spend belonging to repos that are no longer connected.

Their runs are kept forever, so they still count in the global total; this bucket keeps them
attributable.
ArchivedTokens.title: ArchivedTokens

ArtifactCall.description:
One row of a work-item's run call-trail.

`tool_id` pairs a `result` back to its call, and `parent_tool_id` names the sub-agent spawn the row
happened inside.
ArtifactCall.title: ArtifactCall

ArtifactRef.description:
A work-item design artifact, NORMALIZED on read: legacy bare-string and structured entries both
coerce to this shape at the daemon boundary, so the wire contract is never a string-or-object
mix.
ArtifactRef.title: ArtifactRef

ArtifactStatusRow.description:
COMPUTED status of one artifact kind — derived at read time from file existence, self-check and
evidence freshness, so it cannot drift.
ArtifactStatusRow.title: ArtifactStatusRow

AskQuestion.description: One question from a parked grill run — the ask-card's fields, as the reporting tool typed them.
AskQuestion.title: AskQuestion

AssetActionResponse.description: Result of a per-repo asset action (adopt / enable / disable / drop).
AssetActionResponse.title: AssetActionResponse

AssetItem.description: One asset-pool item — `adopted` (in this repo's list) + `enabled` (adopted and not off).
AssetItem.title: AssetItem

AttentionBadge.description: The global badge: the TOP non-empty tier only — one color, one count.
AttentionBadge.title: AttentionBadge

AttentionCard.description:
The what-you-need-to-do card in three parts: WHY, DO, and BASIS.

None when nothing needs the owner, so the card is hidden rather than empty.
AttentionCard.title: AttentionCard

AttentionHold.description: One parked work-item on the top-of-SuperMe attention center.
AttentionHold.title: AttentionHold

AttentionResponse.description: The attention engine's read: strict-priority buckets derived from durable state.
AttentionResponse.title: AttentionResponse

AttentionRow.description:
One item's attention claim: which bucket, why (one human line), and the gate it sits at
(needs_you only).
AttentionRow.title: AttentionRow

AuthStatusResponse.description: Whether SuperMe holds a credential at all. `detail` is the sentence a surface shows.
AuthStatusResponse.title: AuthStatusResponse

AuthorizationRequest.description:
A change to what the project INTENDS that a work-item could not settle alone, awaiting the
owner's grant or deny at review. Every scope is owner-reserved.
AuthorizationRequest.title: AuthorizationRequest

BlockingChild.description:
One open sub-item the parent waits on, resolved to something the owner can read and go to.

A joined id names a thing without saying what it is.
BlockingChild.title: BlockingChild

BoardItem.description: A work-item as it appears on the board — status + dates are the item's own, rendered live.
BoardItem.title: BoardItem

CategoryNode.description:
One node of the semantic tree: a category total, its per-feature amounts, and how it reads.

`label` and `collapsed` are taxonomy decisions, so no renderer re-makes them.
CategoryNode.title: CategoryNode

CheckpointStub.description: One row of the drilldown's continuity feed (newest first) — full text stays behind path.
CheckpointStub.title: CheckpointStub

CompactionConfigBody.description:
Partial update of the compaction runtime; omitted fields stay unchanged. The route refuses any
trigger at or below the incompressible floor.
CompactionConfigBody.title: CompactionConfigBody

ConstitutionEntry.description: One LEARNED universal constitution item (always-on rule) for a mode.
ConstitutionEntry.title: ConstitutionEntry

ConstitutionFileResponse.description: The raw markdown (frontmatter intact) of one constitution — the popup's edit source.
ConstitutionFileResponse.title: ConstitutionFileResponse

ConstitutionToggleResponse.description: ok + slug + scope + the operational toggle result (present/enabled).
ConstitutionToggleResponse.title: ConstitutionToggleResponse

ContextResponse.description: One live context (global or a connected domain) — what the surfaces render.
ContextResponse.title: ContextResponse

Criterion.description:
One rubric criterion, judged. The unit exists because "3 of 4" is not a finding — WHICH one
missed is.
Criterion.title: Criterion

DeputyConfigResponse.description:
The global deputy dial: whether a deputy judges autopilot gates + how readily it escalates
per gate (triage/plan/review, each low·medium·high·extra).
DeputyConfigResponse.title: DeputyConfigResponse

DeputyMandateResponse.description:
The per-repo deputy mandate (the standing acceptance bar). Lives in the harness cell
(`local-harness/<id>/dev/deputy/mandate.md`); seeded from a template on connect, editable here.
DeputyMandateResponse.title: DeputyMandateResponse

DevReadResponse.description: A context's parsed dev knowledge: work-items (enriched) + inbox queue + glance + live runs.
DevReadResponse.title: DevReadResponse

DrilldownAction.description:
One control, with its activation decided SERVER-SIDE.

`reason` is populated either way: greyed it says what would make it live, live it says what
clicking does.
DrilldownAction.title: DrilldownAction

DrilldownResponse.description:
Everything the work-item drilldown renders, computed once per poll.

One computation of the gate's checks, shared with the deputy, so the owner can check its call.
DrilldownResponse.title: DrilldownResponse

EvalMetrics.description:
The artifact's own run cost on a synthetic task.

`run` measures a skill once; `overhead` is a constitution's always-on per-turn cost. Every field
is optional.
EvalMetrics.title: EvalMetrics

EvalReport.description:
A proposal's gate-2 eval report, stored on the row.

Every field is optional, so an older or richer report never 500s a read.
EvalReport.title: EvalReport

ExecutionStep.description: One lifecycle event in a proposal's execution trace (real events + a synthetic 'filed' head).
ExecutionStep.title: ExecutionStep

FoundationFile.description: One universal identity/charter file — SuperMe's repo-agnostic machinery (Foundations).
FoundationFile.title: FoundationFile

GateCheck.description:
One mechanical row of a gate's evaluation, computed from durable state rather than claimed.

`blocking` is the must-resolve marker: a failing one greys Approve.
GateCheck.title: GateCheck

GateNumbers.description: The real-ratio counts (law 2: counts of real things, never invented scores).
GateNumbers.title: GateNumbers

GitHealthResponse.description: One item's live git state — health check + FE decoration (derived, never stored).
GitHealthResponse.title: GitHealthResponse

GitMergeResponse.description:
The review-gate merge. `path` says which route executed: `main` (heavy, with backup ref)
or `parent` (blocking child's light merge into its parent's branch).
GitMergeResponse.title: GitMergeResponse

GitResolveResponse.description:
Resolve-with-Agent accepted: the conflicted sync was left in the item's worktree and a
background resolution run is in flight (poll GET /dev for run state).
GitResolveResponse.title: GitResolveResponse

Glance.description:
The dashboard glance summary (counts + bucketed item stubs). `awaiting_human` is the
attention bucket (the only status that pages the owner).
Glance.title: Glance

GlanceItem.description: A work-item stub in the glance buckets (active / awaiting_human).
GlanceItem.title: GlanceItem

HoldQuestion.description:
One question the grill carries to the owner — the four fields `report_completion` enforces, so the
card renders labelled rows instead of parsing prose.
HoldQuestion.title: HoldQuestion

InboxBriefResponse.description:
One row's handoff brief, the cold-start context the item it becomes reads first.

`editable` is false once pushed: the brief has become provenance.
InboxBriefResponse.title: InboxBriefResponse

InboxRow.description:
One quick-capture triage-queue row. kind/status/origin are locked: DevStore validates
them against its own value-sets on write, so the Literal can't 500 on a real row.
InboxRow.title: InboxRow

KnowledgeNode.description:
A node in the knowledge tree. `dir` nodes carry `children`; `file` nodes omit it
(serialized with response_model_exclude_none so files stay `{name, type, path}`).
KnowledgeNode.title: KnowledgeNode

KnowledgeOkResponse.description: The write/inject result: ok + the (relative) path written.
KnowledgeOkResponse.title: KnowledgeOkResponse

LearningRollupResponse.description:
Per-repo learning counts across the 4-slot pipeline (candidates · pending · drafted · learned),
each split by dev/core scope, plus the cross-repo totals. Powers the Learning tile drill-in.
LearningRollupResponse.title: LearningRollupResponse

LensRead.description:
One standing lens's read of the current cycle.

`probed` separates "nothing is wrong" from "nobody looked", so it is a LIST, one probe per entry,
rendered as one.
LensRead.title: LensRead

LibraryEntry.description:
One proven check the repo keeps.

`standing` attaches to every implementation plan, `available` is cited by id. A plan inherits it
verbatim.
LibraryEntry.title: LibraryEntry

LintFinding.description: One actionable finding over general/. Derived on read — never stored, so it can't go stale.
LintFinding.title: LintFinding

LocalPluginsResponse.description:
A single host's OWN local-harness skills + agents (its `local-harness/<id>/dev` plugin tree) —
flat (no dev/core/shared split; the dev workspace is already mode-scoped).
LocalPluginsResponse.title: LocalPluginsResponse

ManagedConstitution.description:
One constitution for management — dir-scanned (provenance-agnostic: hand-authored + learned
alike), keyed by (scope, slug). Powers the enable/disable surfaces for ALL constitutions.
ManagedConstitution.title: ManagedConstitution

NowStrip.description:
The live phase and cycle, and what that phase concluded.

The phase name and the running dot already say where this is, so no event sentence rides here.
NowStrip.title: NowStrip

Orphan.description: A referential-integrity break — a pointer to an id the anchor docs don't define.
Orphan.title: Orphan

OrphanedRepo.description: A repo id found on disk that the registry does not list and no tombstone explains.
OrphanedRepo.title: OrphanedRepo

OwnerInputBody.description:
The owner's `## From you` section, whole.

Add and delete are both a PUT of the full lists, since the owner is its only writer.
OwnerInputBody.title: OwnerInputBody

OwnerInputResponse.description:
The one section of any report the OWNER writes, re-read from disk after every save.

SLOTS, not prose, so each entry can be added and removed on its own.
OwnerInputResponse.title: OwnerInputResponse

OwnerNote.description:
One thing the owner wants proven. Each becomes a check whose `proves:` is written in their words,
which is why it is one slot and not a paragraph.
OwnerNote.title: OwnerNote

OwnerReference.description: One imported reference the owner handed the plan phase: where it is, and what it governs.
OwnerReference.title: OwnerReference

PagedNotice.description:
Why an item is parked when it is not a plain gate wait.

An escalation, a build⟷vet halt, or a blocked run. None means a normal gate.
PagedNotice.title: PagedNotice

PhaseReportResponse.description:
One phase's user-facing report, plus the path to the agent-facing contract behind it.

The report is the compact read; the contract is one click away, never pasted in.
PhaseReportResponse.title: PhaseReportResponse

PluginEntry.description:
One universal skill/agent in the harness tree. Skills carry `access`; agents carry
`model`/`tools`. Routes use response_model_exclude_unset so each emits only its own keys.
PluginEntry.title: PluginEntry

PluginFileResponse.description: The raw markdown of one skill/agent (popup preview/edit source).
PluginFileResponse.title: PluginFileResponse

PluginScope.description: One scope group (dev | core | shared) in the Skills & Agents tab.
PluginScope.title: PluginScope

PortraitBuild.description:
architecture — only what code CAN'T say. No file trees, no component inventories: those are
stale duplicates by construction. Invariants, boundaries, rationale, and the refusals.
PortraitBuild.title: PortraitBuild

PortraitCapability.description: capabilities — one thing the system can do RIGHT NOW, in user language.
PortraitCapability.title: PortraitCapability

PortraitDeliverable.description:
project-prd — the value statement, not the work. `delivered` is project-level truth (this
value exists now / doesn't yet); sequencing and progress live in the pipeline.
PortraitDeliverable.title: PortraitDeliverable

PortraitGoals.description:
The PRD's goals. `now` must be specific; `direction` may be directional.

Non-goals carry equal weight: what a project refuses is as defining as what it pursues.
PortraitGoals.title: PortraitGoals

PortraitIdentity.description: project-prd — what it is, who for, and the load-bearing field: why it exists.
PortraitIdentity.title: PortraitIdentity

PrCheck.description: One check whose `covers:` names this task, with its recorded verdict joined on.
PrCheck.title: PrCheck

PrCommit.description:
One commit as the walkthrough shows it.

`body` has the SuperMe trailer stripped: that block is what put the commit in this group.
PrCommit.title: PrCommit

PrDiffResponse.description: One file's patches under one task — fetched when the reader opens the row, never up front.
PrDiffResponse.title: PrDiffResponse

PrFile.description:
One file inside a task group, with the churn that group put on it.

Summed over the group's commits, because the biggest change is where the risk is.
PrFile.title: PrFile

PrGroup.description:
One task's slice of the branch. `task` is null for commits with no trailer.

The four fields below the diff are the REVIEW NOTES, per task rather than per file.
PrGroup.title: PrGroup

PrStat.description:
Header numbers: commit count over the fork point, and the NET diff that lands.

Not the sum of per-commit churn: a line written and rewritten lands once.
PrStat.title: PrStat

PrViewResponse.description:
The dedicated PR page: the review report on the left, the task-grouped diff
walkthrough on the right. Entirely derived at read time — nothing here is stored.
PrViewResponse.title: PrViewResponse

ProjectStatusResponse.description:
Whether this project's memory is established.

An un-established repo shows the onboarding front door instead of the work tabs.
ProjectStatusResponse.title: ProjectStatusResponse

PromptExtractionLink.description:
One captured input page for the last probe's phase runs. Survives the probe's teardown, keyed by
the dangling item id.
PromptExtractionLink.title: PromptExtractionLink

PromptExtractionStatusResponse.description: The Prompt X-ray tab's state: a probe in flight (running) + the last probe's captured links.
PromptExtractionStatusResponse.title: PromptExtractionStatusResponse

ProofRow.description:
One row per BUILT THING, each carrying its own validation and verification.

`task: ""` is the item-wide row where untagged content lands, so nothing is dropped.
ProofRow.title: ProofRow

ProofVerdict.description:
One check of the plan's exam: what it will prove, and where it stands.

`ran` False means the loop has not reached it, so approving a plan shows the proof.
ProofVerdict.title: ProofVerdict

Proposal.description:
A memory proposal, a rich DB row with JSON columns.

The declared fields document the stable shape. The enums are locked, since the producer coerces
to them.
Proposal.title: Proposal

ProposalActionResponse.description: reject / drop / artifact-edit: ok + the updated proposal.
ProposalActionResponse.title: ProposalActionResponse

ProposalCandidate.description: A source candidate behind a proposal (provenance shown in the review popup).
ProposalCandidate.title: ProposalCandidate

PublishedDeleteResponse.description: ok + proposal_id + `removed` (the delete_published result) carried via extra.
PublishedDeleteResponse.title: PublishedDeleteResponse

PublishedFileResponse.description: The editable source of a published artifact — its raw markdown + resolved path.
PublishedFileResponse.title: PublishedFileResponse

PublishedRow.description: One published LEARNED artifact, reconciled with live on-disk state.
PublishedRow.title: PublishedRow

PublishedToggleResponse.description: ok + proposal_id + the operational toggle result (present/enabled) spread in via extra.
PublishedToggleResponse.title: PublishedToggleResponse

RepoAttention.description: A repo's holds, grouped so the center can label 'in <repo>'. Only repos WITH holds appear.
RepoAttention.title: RepoAttention

RepoBranchesResponse.description:
This repo's local branches, newest first, work-item branches excluded.

`anchor` is what the anchor resolves to now, so the picker can show the branch in USE.
RepoBranchesResponse.title: RepoBranchesResponse

RepoConnectResponse.description:
A freshly connected repo. `onboarding` is the connect-time choice that its dev workspace launches
until memory is established.
RepoConnectResponse.title: RepoConnectResponse

RepoDisconnectResponse.description:
The receipt for a disconnect — what the cascade removed. Irreversible; the project folder is never
touched, and run traces are preserved.
RepoDisconnectResponse.title: RepoDisconnectResponse

RepoGitResponse.description:
The repo's two git knobs after a write.

`error` when the configured branch does not exist, which every git site refuses rather than
falling back.
RepoGitResponse.title: RepoGitResponse

RepoScope.description: One (repo × scope) cell: home pointers + computed live status + counts.
RepoScope.title: RepoScope

RunEventRow.description:
One entry of a run's event trail: a prompt, a reply, a call, or its result.

`tool_id` pairs a result to its call, `parent_tool_id` names the spawn it sat inside.
RunEventRow.title: RunEventRow

RunHeader.description:
What one of an item's runs WAS, so a call-trail group can name itself.

`feature` answers why a run opened with a shell command instead of a phase skill.
RunHeader.title: RunHeader

RunRow.description:
One row of the spine `run` table, live or historical — shared by every run-returning route.
`feature` stays a free label.
RunRow.title: RunRow

ScopeCount.description: A count split by knowledge scope: dev (repo_dev + universal_dev) vs core.
ScopeCount.title: ScopeCount

SessionDetail.description: One session's title + its most recent bubbles (older ones skipped server-side).
SessionDetail.title: SessionDetail

SessionRenameBody.description: Owner rename of a session. `title` blank/empty ⇒ clear the override (revert to derived).
SessionRenameBody.title: SessionRenameBody

SessionSummary.description:
A session's picker entry.

`item_id` and `item_title` are set when the session is stamped to a work-item, so the chat rail's
indicator is correct however the session was opened.
SessionSummary.title: SessionSummary

SpawnedFrom.description:
The provenance edge, child-side: which item this one branched off and how.

`blocking` and `parallel` gate the parent's completion; `spawn` is provenance only.
SpawnedFrom.title: SpawnedFrom

SweepConfigBody.description: Partial update of the capture-sweep tuning — any omitted field is left unchanged.
SweepConfigBody.title: SweepConfigBody

SweepFamily.description:
One launch button — a projection of `kind_profiles.ResearchFamily`. Only STANDING families
appear: a commissioned one is raised as a ticket about a named subject, so it has no button.
SweepFamily.title: SweepFamily

SystemResponse.description: The System singleton: static config + the live half (in-flight runs) + the repo roster.
SystemResponse.title: SystemResponse

TimelineEvent.description:
One event in a run's trail: a prompt, a reply block, a call, or that call's result — the same rows
the Activity trace shows.
TimelineEvent.title: TimelineEvent

TimelineRun.description: One phase agent's run in the unified timeline: which phase/role it was, and its turn events.
TimelineRun.title: TimelineRun

TokenBucket.description:
A token total plus its splits: `by_category` is semantic, `by_type` systematic, and the two
reconcile. All maps are open, not a locked enum.
TokenBucket.title: TokenBucket

TokenDay.description:
One local-day bucket of the usage time-series: the four token types, the day total, and the
running cumulative.
TokenDay.title: TokenDay

TokenTimeseriesResponse.description: Per-day token usage for the trend graph, bucketed by the caller's local day.
TokenTimeseriesResponse.title: TokenTimeseriesResponse

TokenTypeSplit.description:
The systematic, per-token-type split. A run that never returned a final usage contributes nothing
here — measured usage only. The four sum to the bucket total.
TokenTypeSplit.title: TokenTypeSplit

TokenUsageResponse.description:
System-wide token usage: the global bucket, one bucket per repo, and the roll-up of disconnected
repos.
TokenUsageResponse.title: TokenUsageResponse

VerdictHistory.description: One cycle's verdict for a check — the sequence renders as `c3 ✗→✓`.
VerdictHistory.title: VerdictHistory

WorkGraphEdge.description: One typed edge: contains | spawned_from (carries `relation`) | supersedes.
WorkGraphEdge.title: WorkGraphEdge

WorkGraphNode.description:
One node of the derived WorkGraph. `kind` ∈ repo_root | deliverable | work_item |
inbox_spawn; work_item nodes carry item_kind/phase/status/outcome.
WorkGraphNode.title: WorkGraphNode

WorkItem.description:
A dev work-item. Base fields are always present; tree-walk and telemetry fields appear only on the
enriched list.
WorkItem.title: WorkItem

WorkItemAutopilotResponse.description: Autopilot-toggle result. `changed` False = the flag was already in the requested state.
WorkItemAutopilotResponse.title: WorkItemAutopilotResponse

WorkItemDocEditResponse.description:
Owner edit of `brief.md` or `plan.md`.

`saved` False means the text broke the artifact's contract and NOTHING was written; `issues` are
the lines the gate would refuse on.
WorkItemDocEditResponse.title: WorkItemDocEditResponse

WorkItemGitRecord.description:
The git record a build entry writes onto the item: its branch, worktree dir, and the base it
branched from.
WorkItemGitRecord.title: WorkItemGitRecord

WorkItemScaffoldResponse.description: Result of setting a root work-item's anchor pointer (wave OR deliverable).
WorkItemScaffoldResponse.title: WorkItemScaffoldResponse

WorkItemSeenResponse.description: Seen-stamp result. `changed` False means it was already stamped.
WorkItemSeenResponse.title: WorkItemSeenResponse

WorkItemTimelineResponse.description:
All of an item's runs oldest-first, each with its ordered events — the read-only conversation the
panel mirrors across every phase.
WorkItemTimelineResponse.title: WorkItemTimelineResponse

get.description: Live contexts (global + connected domains) for the surfaces to render.

A context's parsed dev knowledge, inbox queue and glance view.

`running` lists items with a background plan turn in flight, so a card can show planning.

Every item in at most one bucket, by strict priority, derived at read time.

`badge` is the top non-empty tier's colour and count, or null when nothing claims attention.

This repo's decision ledger — every call the owner has ruled on, newest FIRST.

The file is append-only and reads oldest-first, so the order is flipped here and only here.
The anchor-doc set with presence flags (project-prd · spec · roadmap · architecture · resources).
One anchor doc's raw markdown (content is null if the file doesn't exist yet). 404 unknown name.

put.description: Overwrite one anchor doc (creating its folder if needed). 404 on an unknown name.

get.description:
The shared asset pool, each flagged with whether THIS repo has adopted and enabled it.

The pool is shared and adoption is per-repo, so nothing copies a body.

patch.description:
Per-repo asset curation: `adopt` (+ Add), `enable`/`disable` (toggle, keeps adoption), or `drop`
(un-adopt). Writes the repo's `.assets` list — no body copy. Takes effect on the next dev turn.

get.description:
The raw markdown (frontmatter intact) of one constitution — the popup's edit source. The
catalog GET returns only the stripped body + description, so editing pulls the full file here.

put.description:
Save edits to one constitution file, frontmatter kept so `enabled` survives.

Constitutions are read per turn, so it takes effect on the next one.

get.description:
Every constitution in this context's scope: universal-dev + this host's local (`repo_dev`),
each with live `enabled` state. Core is deferred (no core constitutions yet).

patch.description:
Enable or disable any constitution by (scope, slug). No proposal needed.

A disabled one leaves the always-on catalog and becomes unpullable, so it is fully inert.

get.description:
This repo's deputy mandate, the bar it judges gates against while the owner is away.

Seeded from a template on first read, so there is always one to show.

put.description:
Save edits to this repo's deputy mandate. Takes effect on the next deputy dispatch (the mandate
is read per gate); no daemon restart needed.

get.description:
SuperMe's repo-agnostic identity and machinery.

SELF.md is WHO, the per-mode charters are WHAT-MODE, and the learned universal constitution is
what the learning loop published.

put.description:
Save edits to an identity/charter file (SELF.md / dev-charter / core-charter). These are the
hand-authored system-prompt sources; takes effect on the next turn (assembled per turn).

get.description:
This host's OWN local-harness skills + agents (its `local-harness/<id>/dev` plugin tree) — the
per-repo Artifacts tab. Flat: the dev workspace is already dev-scoped, so no scope split.

The raw markdown of one SuperMe skill/agent — the popup's preview + edit source. `scope='local'`
reads this host's own `local-harness/<context_id>/dev` tree.

put.description:
Save edits to one SuperMe skill/agent file (the popup's edit mode). Takes effect on the next
dev turn (plugins are read per-turn); no daemon restart needed for content edits.

get.description:
SuperMe's OWN universal skills and agents, grouped by scope, read straight from the plugin
frontmatter. Per-repo operational artifacts are out of scope here.

The Published inventory — every LEARNED artifact the owner published, reconciled with live
on-disk state (present + enabled). One row per published proposal, newest first.

delete.description:
Remove a published artifact from disk entirely and retire its proposal (history kept). The
loader stops seeing it next turn.

patch.description:
Enable or disable a published artifact at runtime. No delete.

A skill moves between the live plugin tree and its `.disabled/` shadow, effective next turn.

get.description: The raw markdown source of a published artifact — for the Published-tab preview/edit.

put.description: Save edits to a published artifact's source. Takes effect on the next dev turn.

post.description: Quick-capture: add an item to the context's inbox queue (no approval gate).

delete.description:
Remove an inbox item outright (drop = hard delete), including its content folder — unless
the row was pushed (the folder already moved into the work-item's preliminary/).

patch.description:
Edit an inbox item: status, kind, tag, text or title.

A PUSHED row is immutable trace: flipping it back to `open` would let a second push duplicate
it.

get.description:
One row's handoff brief. Agent-filed rows carry one from birth.

`content: null` rather than a 404: an absent brief is a state the owner can still fill.

put.description:
Overwrite one open row's handoff brief, creating it when the row never had one.

409 once pushed: from that moment the brief is the item's provenance.

post.description:
Push an inbox item to the workspace, the owner's push.

One transaction: create the item at triage, move the content in as `preliminary/`, fire
auto-triage.

get.description:
Health of this project's general knowledge, as findings the owner can act on.

Derived fresh on every call, so the lint itself can never be stale.

The activity log, a SELECTIVE read over the events table rather than a dump.

`scope` takes a stored scope or `repo`, which adds the PROJECT's milestones.

post.description:
Fire a background distill pass over the candidate pool.

One pass per repo and scope, guarded by a spine query rather than a shadow set.

get.description:
The review queue: proposals awaiting or past the owner gate, newest first.

Each is enriched with its source candidates, so the review popup can show provenance without a
second round-trip.

post.description:
GATE 1: the owner approves the proposal's INTENT and answers distill's questions.

Fires a background write run that authors the artifact and stages it for gate 2.

patch.description:
GATE 2 (refine) — owner edits the staged artifact before publishing. Only a `drafted` proposal
can be edited; publish then writes whatever is saved here. Status stays `drafted`.

post.description:
The owner DROPS a proposal: this is noise, stop suggesting it.

Unlike reject, dropped candidates are never re-queued.

get.description:
The proposal's lifecycle timeline, reused from the `events` table.

Approve, the forge run, artifact edits, publish. A synthetic head marks where distill filed it.

post.description:
GATE 2 — the owner publishes the staged artifact: the single disk write into its live operational
home.

The proposal must be `drafted`. Core is reserved.

Re-queues its source candidates so a later pass can reframe them. To stop re-suggestion, drop.

Per-repo counts of captured candidates and published artifacts, each split dev and core.

`knowledge` what has been published.

Each carries enough detail to render a popup without a second round-trip.

The chat "/" palette for a (context, mode).

Computed live from disk for the active mode's plugins, merged with the cached external commands.

What this project is, in six bands, one per anchor doc.

Read-only and derived per call: the docs are the store, this is the shape the view needs.

Whether this project's memory is established, with the doc-set flags and onboarding choice.

The workspace gates on `established`: false shows the onboarding front door.

post.description:
Fire a throwaway prompt-extraction probe: a disposable item that runs the real lifecycle
unattended to capture each phase's input, then tears itself down.

One at a time per repo.

get.description:
The repo's current probe state — whether one is running, and the captured input-page links for
the last probe, which survive its teardown.

post.description:
Launch a standing sweep: mint the item at `investigate`, then fire its first run.

An unknown family is a 400, never a research item with no button behind it.

get.description:
The launch bar's buttons, a projection of the research-families registry.

Repo-independent: which sweeps exist is a property of this harness.

The roadmap board: deliverable → wave → its live work-item instances + rollup, plus any
referential-integrity orphans (an item/wave pointing at an id the anchor docs don't define).

post.description:
Force a capture sweep over ONE named session, run to completion.

The everyday triggers are automatic; this is the by-id escape hatch.

Ops hook: force an idle-scan pass now — the same pass the heartbeat runs — with an optionally
lower `idle_seconds`.

get.description:
This repo's standing entries and the available ones a plan cites by id.

A repo with no library reads as two empty lists, the correct starting state.

delete.description:
Drop an entry that turned out not to generalise. The library is knowledge, and knowledge that
proved wrong is removed rather than kept with a caveat nobody reads.

patch.description:
Promote an entry to standing, or demote it back. The OWNER'S call.

A standing entry taxes every future item, which is the one brake on the library accreting.

post.description:
Abandon a work-item. Human-only, legal from any non-terminal phase.

Ordered and each step idempotent, ending with resuming a paused parent.

Approve, and advance a work-item to its kind's next phase.

Refuses at the final phase, on a terminal item, or with a run in flight. Autopilot shares the core.

get.description:
Every tool, sub-agent and skill this item's runs invoked, grouped by run.

`runs` rides along so a group can say what its run WAS, not just "Run #653".

post.description:
The owner's grant or deny on a deferred authorization at review.

Records and routes nothing, so requests can be resolved in any order. `denied` waives the check.

Enrol or un-enrol a work-item in autopilot, the policy that drives its gates without a click.

Allowed only PRE-BUILD, the last moment when flipping it is cheap.

Compact NOW: checkpoint, then `/compact`, then the verdict.

409 without a session or with a run in flight, since the sequence takes the run-lock itself.

get.description:
A work-item's review payload: frontmatter and body, the rendered artifact content, the plan's
`## Tasks` as a structured checklist, and the computed per-artifact status map.

put.description:
The owner hand-edits `brief.md` or `plan.md`, the item's two statements of INTENT.

Refused on a live run, a terminal item, or text failing the artifact's self-check.

get.description:
One of the item's AGENT-FACING artifacts as a standalone page.

`path` is the report's own relative pointer; anything outside the item's `artifacts/` folder is
refused as missing.

Everything the drilldown renders, computed once.

Server-computed activation is the point: a greying rule that lives in the component sits beside the
rule the backend actually enforces.

What the owner has written into the one section of the item that is theirs.

Never 404s: `exists: false` says triage has not written a brief yet.

put.description:
Save the owner's own section, replacing it whole and leaving the rest untouched.

HUMAN-ONLY: the value of the section is that an agent did not write it.
put.summary: Dev Work Item Set Owner Input

get.description:
The item's live git state, derived at read time.

`review_mode` is echoed live, so a mode flip applies to items already at review.

post.description:
The review-gate merge as a raw route, over the same body `advance_item` runs.

Routes by topology: a blocking child merges into its parent's branch, everything else to trunk.

The human decides WHETHER, the agent resolves, and nobody hand-edits conflict markers.

Re-runs the sync leaving conflicts in the worktree, then fires a resolution run.

Restore the trunk to its pre-merge state via the item's recorded backup ref.

Safe-only: refuses once anything else has landed on top. The branch itself is untouched.

get.description:
The dedicated PR page — `strict`'s review surface, and readable in any mode. Read-only
by construction: the page's one action is the ordinary review Approve, which merges.

One file's patches under one task group, fetched when the reader expands the row.

A branch's whole diff is what a review page must not make them wait for.

One phase's user-facing report, plus the path to the contract behind it.

404 when that phase wrote none, so the tab greys itself rather than probing.

post.description:
RE-RUN: throw this item's work away and start it over in place. Destructive.

Artifacts, reports and sessions go; the id, branch, run rows and relations survive.

RESUME a work-item whose run stopped: re-fire the phase's background run.

Nothing is rewound. Distinct from Re-run, which throws the work away.

The owner's manual RUN: fire the current phase's own background run.

For a repo not on autopilot, where every phase would otherwise fire itself.

get.description:
The exact system prompt and body a past run sent, captured at send time, as an HTML page.

A friendly page renders when a run has no capture.

post.description:
Set a root work-item's anchor pointer — `wave` or `deliverable`. Pass one; the other clears to
null.

Stamp the item as SEEN, clearing it from the attention engine's `unread` bucket. A read receipt:
idempotent, never bumps `updated_at`.

get.description:
Every run of this item, oldest-first and phase-tagged with its ordered turn events — the
read-only history the chat panel loads before live-streaming new frames.

The derived work-graph: repo root, deliverables, work-items, unpushed rows and their edges.

Assembled on demand, nothing stored. A cycle is reported as data, never a 500.

picker chooses a project folder. 400 if the path escapes home or isn't a directory.
One knowledge file's text.

knowledge and operational home pointers.

post.description:
Connect a domain: register a new repo into the spine and seed its knowledge home.

`kind` selects its onboarding front door. A new dir is created and must be empty.

delete.description:
Disconnect a domain, forgetting the project entirely. IRREVERSIBLE.

Deletes the registration, knowledge home, harness cell, pipeline state and sessions. The project
FOLDER is never touched, and run rows are preserved.

post.description:
Set this repo's autopilot concurrency cap — the most autopilot items in the build⟷vet loop at
once. Floored at 1.

get.description:
This repo's local branches, the anchor picker's option set.

Read live off git, because a stale list would offer a setting that fails at the next merge.

post.description: Set (or clear) one repo's reasoning-effort override. Clearing falls back to the system default.

Set this repo's review mode and anchor branch, both read live at every decision point.

An anchor naming a missing branch is accepted and reported back as an `error`.
Opt one repo in or out of automatic capture. The global master switch still gates everything.

Set a repo's VISUAL tag: display colour and icon.

Set (or clear) one repo's model override. Clearing falls back to the system default.

The run log: live plus recent history. Scope to one repo with `context_id`, or omit for the
system-wide log.

One run's event trail — the opening prompt, the assistant's reply, and each call, in order.

Per-RUN rather than per-session, so each Activity row has its own thread.

SuperMe's own past CHANNELS for a context, newest first.

ONE ROW PER WORK-ITEM: the owner addresses the ITEM and the phase decides who answers.

Delete a CHANNEL, so a work-item drops all its phase threads.

One tier only: a hard delete of the resumable material. Runs and token trace are preserved.

One session's title and its most recent `limit` replayable bubbles.

`limit<=0` is the whole transcript. The agent always resumes with full server-side context
regardless.

Set (or clear) a session's owner TITLE override. A blank title reverts to the transcript-
derived title. The override is stored on the spine session row and wins in list/read.

runners that take a model from config rather than a per-turn choice.

frontmatter. Send either field; both apply when present.

The top-of-SuperMe attention feed: every `awaiting_human` hold across all connected repos, grouped
by repo and classified.

Only repos with a hold appear; an empty feed means nothing needs the owner.

tool (surface + params). Read-only; introspected fresh on each call so it can't go stale.

unattended.

without a restart.

System-wide token usage: the global total, two reconciling breakdowns, and per-scope and
per-feature splits, the same per repo.
